claim: Western scrub-jays with prior thieving experience re-cache food in new sites after being watched, but not when caching in private (0.44 vs 0.06; Cambridge 0.28 vs 0.08; n=7). Same birds in both sites; tiny n. Gap search: Dally 2006 (Science) shows jays remember which observer watched which caching event; abstract only, no numbers read.
agent_test: Mark items 'exposed' when a prompt or tool log is shared; test whether agent re-verifies exposed items more than private ones at equal tokens.

claim: The Eurasian jay cache-protection effects tied to observer perspective and desire did NOT replicate in the original lab (5 experiments, 14 birds; 4 of 7 directional tests wrong way). Ostojic 2017 and Legg and Clayton 2014 are weakened. Gap search: Dally 2006 itself found no evidence that cache protection is cued by observer behaviour (consistent with the Amodio null). An independent lab (Vernouillet 2025, 6 pinyon jays, 5 nutcrackers) finds pilferer-identity re-caching, not desire-state or perspective effects. No independent replication of Ostojic 2017 found.
agent_test: Treat single small-n animal results as hypotheses; require a replication before turning one into a scaffold rule.

claim: Ravens differentiate knowers from ignorant competitors (informed vs uninformed Wilcoxon n=8 p=0.023; time to pilfer about 10x longer with a dominant non-observer, n=6 p=0.032), but effects are small-n and test-dependent (peephole geometry p=0.297, stay-treatment p=1).
agent_test: Multi-party task with an 'informed' flag per party; compare agent with an explicit knowledge ledger vs none.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Ravens guard caches on hearing conspecifics when a peephole is open but not closed, with no gaze cue (n=9, chi2(2)=14.889 p<0.001; peephole vs non-observed Z=-2.666 p=0.012).
agent_test: Same paper reported twice by two agents; not independent. Needs an independent raven lab.

claim: Apes anticipatory-look to a false-belief location (Exp 1: 20 of 30 looked first at target, P=0.098 alone; combined result significant). The submentalizing control (shapes instead of agents) gave weaker, non-significant results (22 of 43 looked at a box; 14 of 22 on target p=0.28), so the result is open to a low-level reading. Gap search: the anticipatory-looking paradigm failed a 160-infant two-site direct replication of Southgate 2007 (about half looked at the action location in both conditions); Kano 2019 adds an experience-based barrier control in apes (only the opaque-experience group anticipated the mistaken search). No pre-registered large ape replication found.
agent_test: If we use false-belief probes, include a perceptual-cue control version of each item.

claim: Apes pass an active helping false-belief test with an ignorance control: false-belief 72.0% vs ignorance 49.9% (Buttelmann 2017, Study 2; Study 1 76.5% vs 53.1%, N=17 per group). A simple ignorance rule predicts chance, so it is ruled out for this task.
agent_test: Use ignorance-vs-false-belief contrast items to split rule-following from belief tracking.

claim: Chimpanzees pass mistaken-perspective stick game apparently (60% bigger stick) but follow-up showed projection of own preference; chimp results on perspective may reflect egocentric heuristics.
agent_test: Add controls where the target's preference differs from the agent's own.

claim: Rhesus macaques look longer at incorrect search by agents with knowledge (4.34 s vs 3.04 s, t(60)=2.10 p=.04; replication 3.65 vs 2.36 s, n=50), but only for colour change, not size/shape change; effects marginal and method-dependent.
agent_test: Not directly testable; shows boundary-dependent anticipation.

claim: Penn and Povinelli and Heyes: competitive-paradigm and eye-tracking data can be explained by behaviour-reading, submentalizing and learned rules; the field lacks agreed alternatives and discriminating tests. Gap search: Tauzin 2025 applies the same learned-rule critique to bonobo communicative ignorance results.
agent_test: Write the low-level alternative explanation next to every social inference the agent makes.

claim: GPT-4 (June 2023) solved 75% of 40 false-belief tasks (each requiring 16 correct prompts); GPT-3.5 and davinci-003 solved 20%; older models 0%. Verified against arXiv abstract. Counts three records of the same paper.
agent_test: Re-run on current models with Kosinski's reversed and control variants.

claim: LLM false-belief success is brittle: trivial alterations (transparent container, informed protagonist) flip answers; GPT-4 97% on original items falls to 0% on transparent-access and inon categories; double-space prompt change moves probabilities. Gap search 2025-2026: perturbation drops persist in six open models (average 67.2 unperturbed to 35.4 on transparent container under vanilla prompts; Llama 3 70B 100 to 25). In 2025 reasoning models the failures shrink but stay on transparent access and relationship change (Claude thinking, Grok-3-mini, R1 all 0 of 2 items; GPT-5-high 0.5 of 2 on one variant; 14-item hand-scored set).
agent_test: Build perturbation sets for each social-reasoning item; report original and perturbed accuracy.

claim: LLMs state awareness but do not apply it: SimpleToM mental-state question over 95% for GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-405B, Claude-3.5-Sonnet; behaviour prediction at least 30 points lower; judgment 10-25%. Hagendorff: first-order deception 97-99% but second-order only 11.67%. Gap search: SimpleToM v2 (ICLR 2026) shows the gap in GPT-5 (state 98.5, behaviour 64.4, judgment 40.0), o1 (98.6/58.8/32.5), o3-mini (85.4/66.8/41.3); R1 (97.3/73.8/65.8) and o1-preview (95.6/84.1/59.5) are best. The reminder lifts behaviour to 82.8-96.9 for three non-reasoning models; an independent lab sees the same on 8B models (28.9 to 63.2).
agent_test: Ask for the action after state attribution; measure state-to-action gap at equal tokens.

claim: Interactive and conversational ToM is far harder than static: FANToM human ALL 87.5 vs GPT-4 CoT 26.6 (Jun) or 14.8 (Oct); BigToM backward belief false-belief .53; ToMBench gap 10.1 points; SocialIQa 55% and ToMi 60% for GPT-3 (older).
agent_test: Present the same underlying fact in several question types; accept only consistent sets.

claim: Plain chain-of-thought is inconsistent for ToM (ToMBench about 0 gain), while perspective filtering (SimToM: GPT-3.5 BigToM 41.0 to 70.5; ToMi GPT-4 25.5 to 87.75) and symbolic belief graphs (SymbolicToM +62 and +78 points) help a lot. Gap search: a mental-state reminder (the model re-reads its own state answer, about 2 extra tokens) gives most of the SimpleToM recovery; generic CoT of 230 to 298 tokens gives less (GPT-4o behaviour 62.8 vs 82.8). No study compares a belief ledger with SimToM at equal tokens (EnigmaToM and OmniToM do not).
agent_test: Add a 'filter to what X knows' step before answering; compare with CoT at equal tokens.

claim: Adult-level LLM performance on multi-order ToM text Q&A: GPT-4 88.6% vs humans 90.4%; 6th order GPT-4 93% vs human lower. Conflicts in spirit with FANToM and SimpleToM results, because task format differs.
agent_test: Compare same agent on static Q&A versus interactive tasks.

claim: Agent scaffolds with explicit opponent-hypothesis modules (Hypothetical Minds) beat LLM-agent and RL baselines across 30 multi-agent scenarios; ablating hypothesis evaluation hurts. Gap search: an independent team ran Hypothetical Minds in three card and dice games: it beats a vanilla agent in all three (win rate +6.4, +12.8 and +26.0 points) and has the top Goofspiel payoff (+2.836), but it spends 543,649 tokens per Liars Dice game, and in direct play SAGE (a cheaper structured agent) wins 61.7 percent in Goofspiel, ties 50.0 in Liars Dice and loses 30.0 in Leduc.
schema_part: O (hypothesis about other agent scored by prediction)
agent_test: Add an opponent-model hypothesis loop in multi-party tasks.

claim: Scrub-jay-inspired agent memory with perishability gives GenGap +0.108 vs about -0.022 for flat retrieval; decay ablation collapses GenGap 5.7x (2026, author benchmark, 20 instances). Gap search: the same authors also report EventQA-64k (F1 61.58, +2.66 over Mem0); with a stronger backbone a plain dense retriever closes the gap (78.68 vs 72.82) and on conflict-resolution tasks the decay hurts. Still no independent replication.
agent_test: Replicate on independent benchmark; compare against recency baseline.

claim: Animal-cognition methods transfer to LLM tests: ranked-animal prompts vs reverse ranked and random-string controls give different scores (GPT-4o 0.97, 0.78, 0.92 SD .09), showing the value of control conditions. Gap search: control conditions change model rankings. Removing answer options raises R1 on HiToM from 0.549 to 0.691 but lowers non-reasoning Qwen3-8B from 0.557 to 0.510; more reasoning effort lowers o3 from 0.838 to 0.693. RL on small models can give high accuracy via collapsed reasoning (ToM-RL).
agent_test: Use control items in every social-cognition probe.

claim: Longer thinking can hurt social reasoning: GPT-o3 on HiToM falls from 0.838 (lowest effort) to 0.693 (highest); capping Qwen3-8B-Reasoning at 1,500 tokens gives 0.706, above both its modes; an adaptive stop lifts R1-Distill-Qwen-32B from 0.571 to 0.701 on HiToM. No gain on first-order ToMBench.
agent_test: Run the social-reasoning step at several token caps and pick the cap per task type; report accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Frontier-model false-belief perturbation results are scattered: no study found runs the same 2025-2026 model on the Kosinski original items and on Ullman-style perturbed items with the same scoring. Pieces: GPT-5 near perfect on the classic battery (one partial mistake) yet half credit on one transparent-access item; Llama 3 70B 100 unperturbed vs 25 on transparent container.
agent_test: Build one item set with original, reversed, transparent-access and informed-protagonist variants; run the agent on all and report the drop.

claim: Benchmark scores overstate belief tracking: small RL-trained models reach high accuracy with collapsed one-line reasoning (ToM-RL), and reasoning models gain when answer options are removed (R1 +14.2 points on HiToM). Two papers, two labs.
agent_test: Score both the answer and whether the written belief state matches a gold belief list (OmniToM style).

claim: The anticipatory-looking paradigm behind the 2016 ape result failed a close 160-infant, two-site replication of Southgate 2007; a pre-registered large ape replication of Krupenye 2016 was not found by gap search (Crossref, Europe PMC and arXiv queries).
agent_test: Treat ape false-belief evidence as moderate; use the experience-control logic (Kano 2019) when designing agent probes.
